services.hub_choose_title: How to choose between the five
services.hub_choose_body: Most enquiries arrive with a symptom rather than the name of a service, which is perfectly fine. This is the translation: if your opening sentence sounds like one of these, that is the page to read first.

hub_choose_items.when: Clients search for us in Google and do not find us, or there is a site and it brings in no enquiries.
There is a process we do by hand several times a day, where somebody's whole job is moving figures from one place to another.
There is no way to know what is open right now without calling to ask, and it is all run from a spreadsheet that has outgrown itself.
We want to sell online, and the order has to reach the people who fulfil it rather than an inbox somebody remembers to check.
The site is slow, leans on twenty plugins, or the developer who built it has gone and we do not have the code.

services.hub_included_title: What every project includes, whichever service it is
services.hub_included_body: These are not paid extras and not a premium tier. They are how we work, and they are the same for a five-page business site as for an internal system running inside an organisation.
hub_included_items: A twenty-minute scoping call before any proposal, with no commitment and no deck.
A written proposal with scope, stages, date and price - and what is not included, named rather than left vague.
Staged work: at the end of every stage there is something to look at, instead of a reveal at the end.
Accessibility written into the code to the Israeli standard IS 5568, with no third-party widget promising it instead of supplying it.
The code, the domain and the hosting access registered in your name at the end.
The first month of fixes and adjustments included after launch.
And if we are not the right people, you hear that on the first call, with a pointer to who is.
services.hub_price_title: How a price is arrived at
services.hub_price_body: We do not give a number over the phone before seeing the business, because a number like that is a guess both sides then stay attached to. A project usually starts in the low thousands of shekels, and a system with integrations costs more; the exact figure arrives in a written proposal. These are the steps that produce it:
hub_price_items: The scoping call: what is stuck, what already exists, and what should have been happening instead.
A decision on scope: what goes into the first stage and what waits. There is almost always one piece worth building first.
The written proposal: scope, stages, date and price, and what stays out of it.
Timelines: a business site 2-3 weeks, a system 4-6 weeks, from the point the content and the access are in hand.
Each service page carries its own section on what moves the price for that service specifically.

hub_faq_items.question: I do not know which service I need - what then?
hub_faq_items.answer: Get in touch without deciding. Part of the work of the scoping call is saying which of the five this even is, and sometimes the answer is two of them in a particular order. The symptoms above are a better starting point than the name of a service.

hub_faq_items.question: Can several services be combined into one project?
hub_faq_items.answer: Yes, and that is the common case. An online store is a website and an automation at once, and a management system almost always arrives with data to bring across from whatever came before. The proposal is divided into stages, so committing to all of it is never a condition of starting.

hub_faq_items.question: What is the smallest project you take?
hub_faq_items.answer: There is no formal floor. If the budget does not suit a full project we will say what is worth doing with what there is - and sometimes the answer is one stage now and more in six months. Some of our best projects are one-person businesses.

hub_faq_items.question: Will you work alongside our existing suppliers?
hub_faq_items.answer: Yes. A designer, a copywriter, an SEO consultant or a bookkeeper - we build and connect, and we do not ask you to replace anyone already working with you. What we do not do at all is written up on a page of its own.

hub_faq_items.question: Who actually works on the project?
hub_faq_items.answer: We work directly with the business owner, with no layers of account management. That means the answer you get comes from the person doing the building, and it also means the number of parallel projects is limited - which is why we will not promise a timeline we know we cannot meet.

process.section_title: How it works - from brief to build to launch
process.section_subtitle: No surprises and no "we'll get back to you" that never does. Here is exactly what happens once you get in touch

steps.title: Scoping call
steps.description: We work out what your business does, what's stuck, and what the goal is. If we're not the right fit, we'll say so on this call.

steps.title: Proposal and scope
steps.description: One document: what we'll build, what we won't, what it costs and when it goes live. A final price, with nothing added along the way.

steps.title: Development in stages
steps.description: You see a live version in the first week and review as we go. No waiting in the dark until the end.

steps.title: Launch and support

faq.section_title: What a business website costs and how long it takes

items.question: What does a website cost?
items.answer: A business site usually starts in the low thousands, and a complex system with automations and integrations costs more. You'll get an exact range on the scoping call - not before we understand what you need, because any number before that is a guess.

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: A business site: 2-3 weeks. A system with automations: 4-6 weeks. The date is set in the proposal and we hold ourselves to it. If something slips on our side, you hear about it immediately, not at the end.

items.question: Who owns the code and the domain?
items.answer: You do. The domain is registered in your name, the code is handed over, and you are not locked in with us. If you want to continue with another developer you can, and that's completely fine.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: The first month of fixes and adjustments is included. After that you can work with us on a monthly maintenance plan or on demand - no commitment required.

items.question: Do you work with very small businesses?
items.answer: Yes. Some of our best projects have been one-person businesses drowning in manual work. If the budget doesn't stretch to a full project, we'll tell you what is worth doing with what you have.

items.question: What if we're not happy?
items.answer: We stay with it until it works. Working in stages is exactly why - you see output as we go, rather than discovering at the end that we went the wrong way.

contact.call_title: What the intro call looks like
contact.call_body: The first call runs twenty minutes and there is no deck in it. We ask, you describe, and by the end both sides know whether there is a project here. If there is not, you hear that on the call rather than in a follow-up email that never arrives.
call_items: What is stuck today, and how the process actually runs - who types what, where it goes next, where it breaks.
What already exists: a site, a system, a spreadsheet, a WhatsApp group, a paper diary.
What should be happening instead, and which part of that is genuinely blocking you now.
The order to build in. There is almost always one piece worth building first, and it is not always the piece you called about.
contact.deliver_title: What you get after you reach out
contact.deliver_body: Nothing on this list commits you to anything or requires you to sign anything.
deliver_items: A reply within one business day, on the channel you used.
A straight answer on fit. If the work belongs with a mobile studio, a media agency or a copywriter, we name which one.
Once the scope is clear: a written proposal - what gets built, in what stages, by what date, at what price.
What the proposal deliberately leaves out, named rather than left vague.
A plain statement of what is registered in your name at the end: the code, the domain and the hosting access.
contact.response_body: We work across two time zones, Israel and Thailand, so a few hours of offset is the ordinary case here rather than an exception. Thailand runs four to five hours ahead of Israel depending on the time of year, which in practice means a message sent during a Thai afternoon is usually answered the same day, and one sent in a Thai evening is waiting at the start of the next Israeli morning.
response_items: WhatsApp is the fast channel, and the one for a short question.
The form and email are answered within one business day, in the order they arrive.
Friday afternoon and Saturday are the weekend here. A message left then is answered on Sunday.
We work in English and in Hebrew, in writing and on a call, whichever suits you.
fit_yes_items: A manual process that repeats several times a day and eats hours - ordering, work orders, pricing.
Systems that do not talk to each other, so the same figure gets typed in twice or three times.
A site built on a closed platform that you want back as code you own.
A new business site or store, where the point is enquiries rather than presence.
contact.work_body: If you would rather arrive at the call with a clearer picture, two things help: the list of what we build, and real projects you can open and read - what was stuck in each one and what was built for it.

faq_items.question: How quickly do you reply?
faq_items.answer: Within one business day, on the channel you used. On WhatsApp it is usually sooner. An enquiry left on Friday afternoon or Saturday is answered on Sunday, which is the first working day of the Israeli week.

faq_items.question: Can I get in touch before I know what to build?
faq_items.answer: Yes, and that is the common case. A description of what is not working is enough for us to say whether we are the right people. Deciding what to build and in what order is the work of the scoping call, not a condition for having one.

faq_items.question: Does the intro call cost anything?
faq_items.answer: No. Twenty minutes, no commitment and no presentation. If it ends with us looking like the wrong fit, you hear that on the call.

faq_items.question: What should I prepare for the call?
faq_items.answer: Nothing formal. A spreadsheet, a screenshot of the process as it runs today, or a link to the current site will shorten the call, but none of them are needed to have it.

faq_items.question: Do you work with businesses outside Israel?
faq_items.answer: Yes. Part of our work is with a six-branch chain in Thailand, and the interfaces built there are bilingual. We work in English and in Hebrew, in writing and on a call.

faq_items.question: What happens to the details I put in the form?
faq_items.answer: They are used only to get back to you. The form is submitted through Netlify Forms, run by the same provider that hosts this site, and nothing is passed to any other party. The privacy policy spells out the detail.

about.section_title: Building websites for small businesses in Israel
paragraphs: PROPEL was founded on one simple belief: small and mid-sized businesses deserve the same standard of digital execution large corporations get - without corporate pricing and without corporate timelines.

We build systems, streamline processes and grow visibility in Google. We work directly with the business owner, with no layers of account management, and we measure every project by what it changed in the business.

not_a_fit.meta_title: When we are not the right fit
not_a_fit.meta_description: Not every project suits us, and it is better to know before a call than after. What we do not do, and who to ask instead.
not_a_fit.h1: When we are not the right fit
not_a_fit.intro: One of the values we state is that we will tell you what is not worth doing - even when it shrinks our own project. This is the page where that gets tested.
not_a_fit.body: We are not right for every project, and you should know that now rather than after a long call. This list is by TYPE of work, not size of business - some of our best projects are one-person businesses.

items.title: Native mobile apps
items.body: iOS and Android are their own craft, and we have no such project in the portfolio. What we do have: a fast site installable as an app (PWA), which covers a good share of the cases.

items.title: Paid campaign management
items.body: We do organic search - showing up without paying per click. Google Ads and Meta Ads are a different discipline with different logic, and we do not run them.

items.title: Design without the build
items.body: We are not a design studio. Everything we design we also build and ship - which is what keeps us honest about what will look good and also work.

items.title: Building on a closed platform
items.body: We will not build you a new site on WordPress, Wix or Base44. One of our services is getting businesses off them; it is hard to sell that and build another one in the same breath.

items.title: Ongoing content and marketing
items.body: Copywriting, social and email are not us. We build the system the content sits on, and connect it to whoever does that work.

items.title: A project that must ship this week
items.body: A business site takes 2-3 weeks and a system 4-6. We commit to a date up front, so we will not promise a timeline we know we cannot meet.

not_a_fit.instead_body: For a native app, a mobile studio. For campaigns, a media agency. For design alone, a branding studio. For ongoing content, a copywriter or content manager. If it helps, we are happy to point you in the right direction even if we never work together.
not_a_fit.fit_body: If you have a manual process that repeats, systems that do not talk to each other, or a site built on a platform that you want to own - that is exactly us.
